approach: Root cause: reading acceptance (`refusing_check`, crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs:520-551) is an ordered list of `step!` checks, and none compares the request's explicit parts with the reading's deliverables and criteria. No rule says an explicit part stays in scope unless the request defers it. A reading that moves part (3) to `out_of_scope` or a follow-up is therefore accepted (jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k). Fix it at that gate. (1) topics.rs gains a parser `request_parts(text)` beside `request_text_acceptance` and `is_bullet`, which stay unchanged. It reads `N.`, `N)`, `(N)`, `a)`, `(a)` line parts, inline `(1)..(2)..` sequences, and bullets after an `Acceptance:` line. It never reads quoted-evidence lines (`Introspection `, `Cause:`, `Failure class:`, `prevention it proposed:`), so enumerations inside a generated root-cause request's quoted proposals are not parts. (2) checks.rs gains `pub fn check_request_parts(reading, request) -> Result<()>` and one `step!(check_request_parts(reading, request));` line placed LAST in `refusing_check`, so every existing refusal keeps its refusing check. (3) A part is covered when a criterion cites its marker (`(3)`, `part 3`, `item 3`), or when stems pooled from one criterion plus the deliverable paths that criterion names (or one deliverable path alone) share at least min(2, n) stems with the part. A part named only in `out_of_scope` is not covered. (4) A part is exempt only on a job-scope deferral: either its own text, or another request sentence naming its marker, holds a narrow phrase such as 'follow-up job', 'separate job', 'next job', 'later job', 'not in this job', 'deferred to' or 'can wait'. Bare later, future, for now, separately and defer are NOT deferral phrases. The same narrow phrases make a criterion unable to cover a part. (5) Tests in reading.rs and the corpus; a CHANGELOG entry. Enforced by code; no prompt is edited. Revision: all six findings answered. (1) the deferral list is narrowed to job-scope phrases, with cases for '(2) Reject future timestamps' dropped and a covering 'later retries' criterion. (2) quoted-evidence lines are skipped. (3) the stored-reading reuse paths are added to dependents. (4) a request sentence outside the parts can defer a part by naming its marker. (5) a criterion citing the marker, or pooled stems with prefix matching, count as coverage. (6) the helper line references are corrected.

decisions.choice: Add a new parser `request_parts` in topics.rs, returning `RequestPart {marker, text, span}`, and leave `request_text_acceptance`/`is_bullet` unchanged. It skips quoted-evidence lines: lines starting 'Introspection ', 'Cause:', 'Failure class:' or 'Priority:', or holding 'prevention it proposed:'. Inline sequences are read only from the remaining lines.
decisions.reason: `request_text_acceptance` is the parse `athena plan` uses (topics.rs:276, plan_entry at 411) and is also called by steward.rs:587/1566/1582/1658, hestia.rs:1781 and code_health.rs:1348, so changing it would move plan acceptance for queued requests. The corpus pins its bullet counts (`bullets_expected`, refusal_corpus.rs:2788-2794) and pins 0 for `N)` and `(a)` parts as a known gap (refusal_corpus.rs:1891-1918). Generated root-cause requests quote each introspection's proposal on a line starting 'Introspection {id} (job {job}); prevention it proposed: ...' (hestia.rs:1041, 'Failure class:' at 1025). A proposal that enumerates '(1) add a check, (2) edit the prompt, (3) ...' must not become required parts, because the root-cause default lets the reader reject a proposal and fix the cause another way. Skipping those lines answers finding 2 and also avoids '...'-truncated last parts.

rejected.why: It changes the plan acceptance of every queued request and the bullet counts the corpus pins.

rejected.option: Read inline sequences from the whole request, with only a marker-list-without-text guard.
rejected.why: A quoted proposal with text after each marker passes that guard and would be required as parts; the quoted lines must be excluded.

decisions.choice: Place the step last in `refusing_check`, after `check_reading_references`.
decisions.reason: Every existing refusal case keeps the check that refuses it, because the new step runs only when all others pass. `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` anchors on the `check_reading_references` step line (refusal_corpus.rs:2927) and still works. Only Accept cases with explicit parts can change.

rejected.why: It would pre-empt refusals such as `check_outcome_state` in the delivery cases that carry `2)` and `(a)` parts (refusal_corpus.rs:936-949) and change the refusing check of existing cases.

decisions.choice: Count explicit enumerated parts anywhere (outside skipped quoted lines), and `-`/`*`/`N.` bullets only after a line equal to `Acceptance:` (case-insensitive).
decisions.reason: The failure class is a dropped enumerated part such as (3); acceptance bullets are the second introspection's proposal. Many existing tests run the real gate with short dash-bullet requests and scripted readings (reading.rs:2638, 2753, 2951; drain.rs:3988, 4067, 6320; job_plan.rs:166), and a free-form dash bullet is not a named part.

rejected.option: Treat every dash or star bullet as a part.
rejected.why: Larger blast radius over fixtures this planner cannot run, and a false-refusal risk on bullets a reader legitimately rewords.
It leaves out the request acceptance bullets that criterion 3 and introspection 20261029-111141-1661 name.

decisions.choice: The deferral list `DEFER_PHRASES` holds only phrases that move a part to other work: 'follow-up job', 'follow up job', 'in a follow-up', 'in a follow up', 'as a follow-up', 'as a follow up', 'separate job', 'next job', 'later job', 'not in this job', 'deferred to', 'can wait'. It is matched by `has_phrase` (whole words, surveys.rs:39) on lowercase text. Bare later, future, for now, not now, separately, afterwards, defer and out of scope are dropped. The phrases are used for two tests: a part exempt by deferral, and a criterion that cannot cover a part.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. Ordinary parts like '(2) Reject future timestamps', '(1) List each file separately' and '(3) Defer the flush until exit' must stay required; 'Later retries reuse the cache' and 'future runs skip it' must still count as coverage. Multi-word job-scope phrases do not occur in ordinary requirements. 'deferred to' is kept because it names a destination. The list is a known limit: a deferral worded otherwise is refused, and the reader's one re-read plus the error text give the repair.

rejected.option: Keep the broad list and apply it to criteria.
rejected.why: It exempts real parts and throws out good criteria (finding 1).

A reader could write 'part (3) follows in a follow-up job' as a criterion to cover a drop; the narrow phrases make that refusable at no cost to ordinary criteria. The corpus case `request-parts-covering-criterion-says-follow-up` pins it.

decisions.choice: A part is also deferred by the request when a request sentence outside every part span and outside the skipped quoted lines holds a `DEFER_PHRASES` phrase and cites the part's marker as `(N)`, `N)`, `part N`, `item N` (for letters `(c)`, `part c`, `item c`). `RequestPart` carries a byte span so the parts are blanked before the request is split into sentences on newlines and '. '.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4. Criterion 4 of the brief says 'unless the request text itself defers it'; a sentence like 'Part 3 can wait for a follow-up job.' after the parts is the request deferring. Blanking the part spans stops an inline sequence ending 'in a follow-up job' from deferring every part it contains.

rejected.option: Check only the part's own text.
rejected.why: It wrongly refuses a reading that follows a request deferring the part in a later sentence.

decisions.choice: Coverage: a part is covered when (a) a criterion that does not itself hold a `DEFER_PHRASES` phrase cites its marker (`(N)`, `part N`, `item N`, `(c)`, `part c`; not bare `N)`), or (b) the stems of one criterion pooled with the stems of every deliverable path whose text the criterion contains share at least min(2, n) stems with the part, or (c) one deliverable path alone shares at least min(2, n) stems. `out_of_scope` never covers. Stems: lowercase alphanumeric words of 3 or more letters, trailing `s` dropped when the word has more than 3 letters, cut to 6 chars, minus `COMMON_WORDS` (topics.rs:156-215) and `PART_FILLER` (`pass`, `cargo`, `clippy`, `fmt`). Two stems match when equal or when the shorter, of at least 3 chars, is a prefix of the other.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 5. Part '(2) Document the flag in the guide' has stems {docume, flag, guide}; the natural criterion '[content] docs/guide.md describes --json' has {doc, guide, json, descri} after the new 3-letter rule and prefix match ('doc' is a prefix of 'docume'), so it shares 2 and is covered; a criterion saying 'covers part (2)' is covered by the marker. A part reduced to a vague line still shares too few stems, which gives 'narrows' a testable form. The producer states the stems of the corpus case in its comment, and if a stem the case relies on is in `COMMON_WORDS` or the rule gives a different count, repairs the case text, not the threshold.

rejected.option: Require a deliverable and a criterion for every part.
rejected.why: A docs or study part may be met by a criterion alone, and deliverable paths rarely carry the words of a part.

rejected.option: Count shared words across the whole reading text.
rejected.why: Summary and title echo the request, so a dropped part would still look covered.

rejected.option: Keep 4-letter stems and a threshold of 2 within one criterion.
rejected.why: It refuses the reworded docs/guide.md shape (finding 5).

decisions.choice: Enforce by code only; edit no prompt.
decisions.reason: The reader prompt budget is 1998 of 2000 (docs/system-facts.md budget line). The refusal text reaches the reader on its one corrected re-read (`read_for` passes the refusal back, reading.rs:720-759).

rejected.option: Add a rule line to the reader prompt.
rejected.why: There is no token headroom, and prose is not a mechanism.

risks.risk: False refusals of good readings, because a reader rewords a part so it shares fewer than min(2, n) stems with any criterion.
risks.mitigation: Parts with no significant stems are skipped; short generic gate bullets (fmt, clippy, test pass) are filtered by `PART_FILLER`. A criterion citing the marker covers the part. Stems pool one criterion with the paths it names and match by prefix. The error names the part and the repair, and the reader gets one corrected re-read (reading.rs:738-759). The 10% share is declared as an estimate; Athena's replay measures it at verification, and the planner cannot run it because `records/` is absent.

risks.risk: An existing test with a scripted or stored reading and a request that has an `Acceptance:` line or enumerated markers is newly refused, forcing edits outside the five listed deliverables (reading.rs:7396, 7743; steward.rs:2585-2639; run/tests.rs; drain.rs).
risks.mitigation: Dash bullets count only after an `Acceptance:` line, and the search found no enumerated markers in requests outside the corpus. The producer runs `cargo test --locked`, `cargo test -p athena-core steward::tests` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` before finishing and repairs the scripted reading's criteria, never the check, naming any such file in the report.

risks.risk: Enumerations in quoted evidence of generated root-cause requests, or a marker list in prose such as 'such as (1), (2) and (3)', are read as parts.
risks.mitigation: Quoted-evidence lines are never parsed. An inline sequence counts only when every marker has text with a significant stem, and the last part ends at the first sentence end. Corpus cases `request-parts-quoted-proposal-enumeration-ignored` and `request-parts-marker-list-without-text` pin both.

risks.risk: The narrow deferral list misses a real deferral worded another way, so a reading that follows the request is refused.
risks.mitigation: The error text names the part and says the request itself must defer it; the reader's re-read can cite the part in a criterion. The list is stated as a known limit in the doc comment. Preferring a refusal the reader can repair over silently exempting ordinary words.

risks.risk: The recorded request text of jobs sza7 and bw7k is not available to the planner, so the corpus shapes are rebuilt from the introspections' account.
risks.mitigation: The case `source` strings say 'rebuilt from the introspection's account', not 'verbatim'. The test of criterion 2 holds the property for any part (3), not for one job.

risks.risk: Prefix matching of 3-letter stems and the 6-character cut can match unrelated words, so a dropped part is judged covered.
risks.mitigation: Coverage needs 2 shared stems within one criterion (plus its named paths), or a cited marker. This is a known limit stated in the doc comment; it is a heuristic like the sibling checks.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in reading.rs. It runs `check_request_parts` on the part-three-moved-to-out_of_scope reading from criterion 2 and takes `unwrap_err().to_string()`, asserting it contains the marker `(3)`, the part's words ('timeout test'), 'out_of_scope' or 'follow-up' as the cause, the repair 'deliverable and a criterion', and the exemption 'request itself defers'. A second case uses a request whose part (3) reads '(3) Add a dashboard in a follow-up job', and a third a request with '(1)..(3)' followed by the sentence 'Part 3 can wait for a follow-up job.', each with a reading that omits part 3: `check_reading_acceptance` is Ok. Further cases show '(3) Add a latest-value column', '(3) Reject future timestamps', '(3) Defer the flush until exit' and '(3) List each file separately' are NOT deferred (a reading that omits them is refused), and that a covering criterion 'Later retries reuse the cache' still covers.
demonstrations.observes: The refusal names the part and the repair; a request that defers the part with a job-scope phrase, in the part or in a later sentence, is accepted; words that merely resemble deferral do not defer.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check, `unwrap_err()` panics because the function is absent or returns Ok, so the first assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Run Athena's three checks on the final tree as separate simple commands: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`. The producer, before finishing, also runs `cargo test -p athena-core`, `cargo test -p athena-core steward::tests`, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` and `cargo test -p athena-cli`, and repairs any pre-existing fixture whose scripted or stored reading is newly refused by `check_request_parts` (repairing the fixture's criteria, never the check), naming the file in the report. The tree under test contains the new check, the new reading.rs tests and the new corpus cases, so `cargo test --locked` exercises criteria 1-7 as well as every old test.
demonstrations.observes: `cargo test --locked` exits 0 with the new unit tests, the corpus tests (including the self-check that `check_request_parts` has a refusing case) and every pre-existing test passing; `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` also exit 0.

If the check newly refused a scripted or stored reading in an existing test (reading.rs, steward.rs, drain.rs, job_plan.rs, run/tests.rs), that test fails; unformatted code fails `fmt --check`; a warning in the new code fails clippy `-D warnings`.
